subdomain: 6.3 Manage stakeholder feedback loops and expectation alignment (including SLAs)

en.question: A port-incident briefing pilot has a signed expansion gate: at least 97% usable briefs in each supported language and no unresolved severity-one feedback, meaning a confirmed omission capable of misdirecting incident response. The overall rate is 99%, one language is at 92%, and a verified severity-one omission remains open. Availability meets its separate service level agreement (SLA). Which actions follow the agreed stakeholder process? Select 2 answers.

options.text: Approve expansion using the overall usable-brief rate because the separate availability SLA establishes that the service is operating within its commitments.
options.note: Aggregate quality and availability do not satisfy the explicit per-language quality gate or close the unresolved severity-one omission.

options.text: Hold expansion and inform the accountable approver that both the language-specific quality condition and the unresolved-feedback condition have failed.
options.note: The agreement makes these independent expansion conditions; a green availability metric cannot offset either failure.

options.text: Assign the omission to domain and product owners, add the adjudicated case to acceptance checks, and communicate evidence required for closure.
options.note: Owned adjudication, testable remediation, and clear closure evidence connect the confirmed feedback to the existing acceptance gate.

options.text: Replace the language-specific gate with the observed aggregate rate for this release, recording the language issue as a future optimization opportunity.
options.note: Retroactively substituting an easier metric bypasses the signed expansion conditions instead of resolving or formally renegotiating them.
